# jsonstor-duckdb

> Home: [http://jsonstor.liquicode.com](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com)
>
> Version: 0.1.0

### Documents are stored in a DuckDB database.

Overview
---------------------------------------------------------------------

`jsonstor` defines one interface for working with a document store and implements it
  for a variety of database products and file formats. The interface is the same whichever
  adapter is underneath, so the storage a project uses becomes a configuration decision
  rather than a structural one.

This package is one such adapter. Documents are stored in a DuckDB database.

***It is packaged separately so that it stays optional.*** A project which does not store
  documents this way never downloads [`@duckdb/node-api`](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb-node-neo).

See [`@liquicode/jsonstor`](https://github.com/liquicode/jsonstor) for the interface,
  and [jsonstor.liquicode.com](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com) for the documentation.

Getting Started
---------------------------------------------------------------------

```bash
npm install --save @liquicode/jsonstor-duckdb
```

```js
const jsonstor = require( '@liquicode/jsonstor' )();
jsonstor.LoadPlugin( require( '@liquicode/jsonstor-duckdb' ) );

let storage = jsonstor.GetStorage( 'jsonstor-duckdb', {
	Database: '...',
	Schema: "main",
	Table: '...',
	IdField: "",
	ModifySchema: false,
	PayloadColumn: "",
	PayloadSync: false,
	Columns: [],
} );
```

Settings
---------------------------------------------------------------------

| Setting | Required | Default | Description |
|---|:---:|:---:|---|
| `Database` | ***Yes*** | - | The database to open: a file path, or `":memory:"` for one which lives only as long as the storage. |
| `Schema` | No | `"main"` | The schema holding the table. Every statement names it, so the connection's search path does not decide which table is used. |
| `Table` | ***Yes*** | - | The name of the table to use. |
| `IdField` | No | `""` | The column to treat as the document identifier. Empty means none. |
| `ModifySchema` | No | `false` | Allow the adapter to create the schema, the sequence, the table, and the columns it is told to create. It never adds a column because a document had a field. |
| `PayloadColumn` | No | `""` | The column which stores the document as JSON text. Empty means none, and then every field must already be a column. Created when missing if `ModifySchema` is `true`. |
| `PayloadSync` | No | `false` | Store the whole document in the payload, making the other columns an index over it. When `false` the payload holds only the fields which have no column. |
| `Columns` | No | `[]` | Columns to create, as `{ Name, Type, Key }`. Used only when this adapter creates the table; afterwards the table itself is the authority. |

Peculiarities
---------------------------------------------------------------------

- ***A criteria becomes a `WHERE` clause ***and*** is handed to `jsongin`.*** The clause is a pre-filter which decides how many rows leave the database; `jsongin.Query` then decides which of them match. So an operator `SqlExpression` cannot translate is ***left out of the statement rather than refused***, and the result broadens: more rows travel, and the answer is the same one every other adapter gives. What that costs, and which operators it applies to, is described in [Translation Layer](/guides/Translation-Layer.md).
- ***The table is an index over the document, not the document.*** Real columns are what the `WHERE` clause can filter on; the `PayloadColumn` carries the document itself. ***Which of three configurations you get is decided by two settings:***
  - ***No `PayloadColumn`.*** The document *is* the columns. A field with no column, or a value SQL has no form for, is ***refused by name*** rather than dropped. Use this to store flat documents in a table you already have.
  - ***`PayloadColumn` with `PayloadSync: false`.*** The columns hold the fields they have, and the payload holds everything else. Nothing is duplicated, and a column another application writes stays visible to jsonstor.
  - ***`PayloadColumn` with `PayloadSync: true`.*** The payload holds the whole document and the columns become an index over it. ***This is the only configuration which answers every question the other adapters answer***, because the payload is real JSON: an absent field stays apart from one holding null, a number does not come back a string, and an object keeps its field order.
- ***A column which mirrors the payload is filtered on, then checked again.*** Under `PayloadSync: true` a value which does not fit its column is stored as `NULL` there and kept in the payload, so every condition on such a column is widened to admit `NULL` and `jsongin` decides the row from the payload. The clause narrows the search; it never narrows the answer.
- ***There is no server, and that is the main practical difference from the other SQL adapters.*** DuckDB runs inside your process. `Database` is either a file you name or `":memory:"`, there is nothing to install and nothing to authenticate against, and a storage cannot fail because something was not running.
- ***A file database and an in-memory one are held differently, and you do not have to care which.*** An in-memory database *is* its connection, so the adapter opens one and keeps it; a file outlives any connection, so the adapter opens and closes one per statement and leaves no handle behind. The only visible consequence is the obvious one: `":memory:"` is discarded when your process ends.
- ***DuckDB is strict where sqlite and MySql are forgiving, in the same two ways PostgreSql is.*** It converts a value which does not match its column rather than storing it as given, and it refuses a comparison whose operand is not the column's type rather than coercing one side. Both are handled and neither costs you an answer: ***a value which does not fit its column is stored as `NULL` there and kept in the payload***, and ***a condition whose operand disagrees with the column is left out of the clause*** and decided by `jsongin` instead. The only cost is that such a query reads more rows.
- ***A fractional number does not fit an integer column***, and this is the case worth knowing about because SQL would otherwise round it silently. `3.14` written to an `INTEGER` column would be stored as `3` and a later search for `3.14` would not find the row. It is stored as `NULL` in the column and kept exactly in the payload, so the search finds it. The same applies to a number too large for its column.
- ***A `VARCHAR` length is not a constraint here.*** DuckDB accepts a string longer than a column's declared length and stores it whole, so `VARCHAR(5)` and `VARCHAR` behave identically. Declare the length for documentation if you like; nothing enforces it.
- ***The payload column is `VARCHAR` rather than DuckDB's `JSON` type.*** A parsed form returns its own key order, so a query comparing a whole object would be comparing a document you did not write. `VARCHAR` returns the bytes which were stored. This costs the ability to index into the payload, which is a trade this adapter has not taken yet.
- ***Two differences remain in the configurations which have no payload for a field:***
  - There is no way to store `undefined`. A query matching a field against `undefined` always fails.
  - A field missing from an insert is filled with the column default, so an absent field and one holding `null` read back the same. Set `PayloadSync: true` if that distinction matters.
- ***`ModifySchema: true` lets the adapter alter your database.*** It creates the schema, a sequence, the table, the columns named in `Columns`, and the `PayloadColumn`. ***It never adds a column because a document had a field***, so your schema is what you declared rather than a record of whatever was inserted first. Think before enabling it against anything you care about.
- ***A table this adapter creates has a `VARCHAR` `_id`, a `_seq` column, and a sequence behind it.*** Your `_id` is taken as given and one is minted when you omit it, the way every other adapter behaves. `_seq` records insertion order, because a `SELECT` with no `ORDER BY` promises none and DuckDB has no row identifier which survives an update; it is never part of a document. ***Dropping the storage drops the sequence too***, so a rebuilt collection counts from one again. A table you bring yourself has no `_seq` and is read in the database's order.

Storage Interface
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Every adapter implements the same functions, and they are documented once:
  [Storage Interface](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com/#/guides/Storage-Interface.md).

***The operator list is not repeated here.*** A criteria, a projection, and an update are
  the engine's, and the list changes whenever the engine gains an operator - a copy in this
  file could only ever be out of date. See the
  [Operator Reference](https://github.com/liquicode/jsongin/blob/main/docs/guides/Operator-Reference.md).

Dependencies
---------------------------------------------------------------------

- [`@duckdb/node-api`](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb-node-neo) : The official DuckDB client for Node.
- [`@liquicode/jsonstor`](https://github.com/liquicode/jsonstor) : The storage interface.
- [`@liquicode/jsongin`](https://github.com/liquicode/jsongin) : The query engine.
